website.quote: We are working together to build the world’s most sophisticated particle detector for analyzing collisions between electrons and protons or other nuclei.

name: ePIC
notes: ePIC is NOT an upgrade of STAR: it replaces STAR in the same interaction region (STAR was taken apart to make way for it); no lineage row is recorded.

The EIC project detector was selected in 2022 from the ATHENA, CORE and ECCE proposals (ECCE adopted as the reference design in March 2022 per a 2023 ePIC talk, not cited); ePIC was formed in July 2022.
A second EIC detector at another interaction region is discussed (EIC Yellow Report: "two complementary detectors") but is not an experiment with a host site and design report; it is not recorded.

physics_goals.quote: The ePIC detector at the Electron-Ion Collider will study these components with unprecedented precision, providing new insights, especially into the behavior of sea quarks and gluons.
physics_goals.value: Study the quark-gluon structure of nucleons and nuclei, especially sea quarks and gluons, with polarised electron beams

summary.plain: ePIC is the first detector for the Electron-Ion Collider. A compact, multi-layer detector with a big solenoid magnet, it will record the particles produced when electrons hit protons and nuclei, so physicists can image the quarks and gluons that make up visible matter.
summary.technical: ePIC (electron-Proton/Ion Collider detector): general-purpose EIC project detector built around a 1.7 T, 2.8 m bore superconducting solenoid, with silicon (MAPS) and micro-pattern gas tracking, fast-timing and Cherenkov PID, electromagnetic and hadronic calorimetry, covering about 3-177 degrees centrally (|eta| < 3.5) plus far-forward and far-backward detectors extending the acceptance to |eta| > 6; to be installed at the former STAR interaction region of RHIC.

unique_capabilities.quote: The ePIC detector instruments state of the art detector technology to provide precision momentum, energy and particle identification over a large acceptance.
unique_capabilities.value: Large-acceptance central detector (about 3 to 177 degrees) with far-forward and far-backward detectors extending the acceptance beyond |eta| of 6
